detailed_findings.finding: Forward implication is complete: polynomiality of P gives N = D P, so root multiplicities at primitive d-th roots of unity yield the required floor inequality for every positive d.
Converse implication is complete: the assumed floor inequalities give multiplicity domination for every root of D, which is enough to conclude D divides N in C[q] by linear factorization over C.
The integrality step is justified: because D is monic and N,D are in Z[q], long division produces Q,R in Z[q], and divisibility over C[q] forces R = 0.

reason: The proof establishes both directions of the claimed equivalence. It correctly rewrites the product as N(q)/D(q), counts multiplicities of primitive d-th roots of unity in N and D via the floor expressions, derives the inequality from polynomiality in the forward direction, and in the converse shows that all roots of D occur in N with at least the same multiplicity, hence D divides N over C[q]. The final step from divisibility over C[q] to a quotient in Z[q] is justified by monic long division in Z[q]. The argument matches the lemma's semantic role exactly and appears self-contained.
